phenomena.claim: Macroscopic thermodynamic irreversibility / arrow of time
phenomena.source: archive: origin/v4:program/REALITY_PICTURE_01.md LEVEL 0 item 7 'Thermodynamic irreversibility / arrow of time [E]'
phenomena.caveat: the phenomenon is observed; its explanation carries the boundary-condition input recorded under empirical_inputs

phenomena.claim: Isolated quantum many-body systems relax to states described by equilibrium statistical mechanics (equilibration/thermalization), with the eigenstate-thermalization mechanism: a single many-body eigenstate suffices to compute thermal averages
phenomena.source: Rigol, Dunjko & Olshanii, Nature 452, 854 (2008), arXiv:0708.1324 — abstract verified 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: generic non-integrable systems; the ETH mechanism is COMMUNITY-DERIVED hypothesis-grade, not a theorem; integrable and many-body-localized systems are recorded exceptions (see open_problems)

phenomena.claim: Fluctuation-theorem statistics are observed in single-molecule nonequilibrium experiments (Crooks theorem verified; folding free energies recovered from irreversible work)
phenomena.source: Collin, Ritort, Jarzynski, Smith, Tinoco & Bustamante, Nature 437, 231 (2005) — title/authors/venue/claim verified 2026-09-23 via PubMed 16148928 and publisher listing

formalism.claim: Equilibrium described by ensembles (microcanonical/canonical/grand canonical); the partition function generates thermodynamic potentials; entropy = state-counting over coarse-grainings
formalism.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 1 'Entropy = state-counting over coarse-grainings — effective-layer [T]'; textbook-standard
formalism.caveat: Stage 2 cheap primary cite: Gibbs, Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics (1902)

formalism.claim: Fluctuation-dissipation theorem: equilibrium fluctuation spectra determine linear response; quantum form G_K(omega) = coth(hbar*omega/2kT)(G_R - G_A)
formalism.source: Callen & Welton, Phys. Rev. 83, 34 (1951); Kubo, Rep. Prog. Phys. 29, 255 (1966) — both abstract-verified 2026-09-23

formalism.claim: KMS condition characterizes thermal equilibrium states and is equivalent to passivity (no work extractable in cyclic processes) for beta > 0 — the second law as a property of the state
formalism.source: Pusz & Woronowicz, Commun. Math. Phys. 58, 273-290 (1978) — title/authors/venue/year verified 2026-09-23 at Project Euclid; content statement carried by archive origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md section 2
formalism.caveat: external verification is at metadata level (abstract paywalled); complete-passivity fine print and the KMS primary chain (Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570 (1957); Martin & Schwinger, Phys. Rev. 115, 1342 (1959); Haag-Hugenholtz-Winnink, Commun. Math. Phys. 5, 215 (1967)) deferred to Stage 2

formalism.claim: Nonequilibrium work relations: Jarzynski equality <exp(-beta W)> = exp(-beta dF) and the Crooks entropy-production fluctuation theorem for microscopically reversible stochastic dynamics
formalism.source: Jarzynski, Phys. Rev. Lett. 78, 2690 (1997), arXiv:cond-mat/9610209; Crooks, Phys. Rev. E 60, 2721 (1999), arXiv:cond-mat/9901352 — abstracts verified 2026-09-23

formalism.claim: The GRUT archive operationalizes detailed balance as an executable admission gate: a (chi, noise) kernel pair passes iff it satisfies the quantum FDT/KMS relation on a frequency grid; white-noise / temperature-independent kernels FAIL; T <= 0 is rejected as KMS-undefined
formalism.caveat: PROGRAM machinery note, not a physics claim: hbar = k_B = 1, bosonic Gaussian bath, max-relative-residual tolerance check; in-house and unreviewed

primitives.claim: A probability measure over microstates (equal a priori probabilities / typicality, or an assumed bath state) is a primitive of the statistical description, not derived from the microdynamics
primitives.source: archive: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md section 4 'No surveyed derivation escapes a low-entropy/typicality input — Bogoliubov's weakening-of-correlations and ETH/typicality merely relocate it'; REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 1
primitives.caveat: survey-scoped statement, not a theorem over all possible derivations

derived_objects.claim: The second law (entropy increase in irreversible adiabatic processes between equilibrium states) is derivable from axioms of adiabatic accessibility, with temperature derived from entropy
derived_objects.source: Lieb & Yngvason, Phys. Rep. 310, 1-96 (1999), arXiv:cond-mat/9708200 — abstract verified 2026-09-23
derived_objects.caveat: equilibrium states; comparison principle assumed within the axiom set

derived_objects.claim: The third law's zero of entropy is grounded in the empty system: the empty system is the zero for system composition and 'we can therefore use the empty system as our zero reference for entropy'
derived_objects.source: Carcassi & Aidala, 'Reverse Physics: From Laws to Physical Assumptions', Found. Phys. 52, 40 (2022), arXiv:2111.09107 — full-text extraction 2026-09-23 (quotes on empty system as compositional zero and entropy zero-reference)
derived_objects.caveat: a Reverse-Physics conceptual grounding, presented by the authors as conceptual necessity rather than the phenomenological crystalline-reference statement

derived_objects.claim: Existence and magnitude of dissipation are intrinsic to the in-in / influence-functional reduction (retarded analytic self-energy, positive Kallen-Lehmann spectral measure, positive-semidefinite noise kernel), requiring no low-entropy system initial state
derived_objects.caveat: recorded scope: Gaussian baths, in-in/Feynman-Vernon reduction; the archive's own anti-laundering note records that positivity is established relative to a passive/stable reference state, so the import is partly co-supplied; in-house, unreviewed

empirical_inputs.claim: In every surveyed account the arrow of time is obtained only by supplying a boundary condition: the low-entropy past boundary (Past Hypothesis) enters as INPUT, not as a derived consequence of dynamics
empirical_inputs.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 3 edge 'arrow-of-time ──REQUIRES──▶ boundary condition [T] INPUT (the past hypothesis) — origin UNRESOLVED'; Q17 minimum input set includes 'initial condition'
empirical_inputs.caveat: Stage 2 cheap community cite: Albert, Time and Chance (Harvard UP, 2000); Boltzmann's original formulation. Claim wording softened by the verification pass 2026-09-23: the archive's REQUIRES edge label is not repeated here as an assertion (requirement stamps are Stage 4's job, CORPUS_SCHEMA rule 4); the verbatim edge is carried under known_connections with its vocabulary disclaimer

empirical_inputs.claim: Within the tested reductions, the direction of relaxation is state-dependent, never dynamics-intrinsic: for equilibrium KMS baths it is fixed by sign(beta) of the assumed passive past-boundary state; the three guises (contour endpoint, KMS passivity, factorized rho_S x rho_B) reduce to one initial-condition assumption
empirical_inputs.source: archive ref: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md sections 2, 5 and honest ledger
empirical_inputs.caveat: recorded scope: equilibrium KMS and surveyed non-equilibrium/NESS bath classes — 'a scoped result, not a universal no-go theorem'; in-house, unreviewed

constants.claim: Boltzmann constant k_B = 1.380649 x 10^-23 J/K, exact by the 2019 SI redefinition (it defines the kelvin)
constants.source: CODATA 2022 via NIST constants database (physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?k) — fetched 2026-09-23, listed '(exact)'
constants.caveat: since 2019 a defined conversion factor, not a measured quantity; pre-2019 measurement chain is the empirical content

symmetries.claim: The relevant microscopic dynamics are time-reversal symmetric; irreversibility is not supplied by the dynamical laws (Loschmidt)
symmetries.source: archive: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md sections 1, 3 (exact demonstration: dephasing function Gamma(t) = Gamma(-t) identically; 'Microscopic dynamics ... distinguish no direction of time')
symmetries.caveat: weak-interaction T violation exists in the SM but is not on record as supplying the thermodynamic arrow; that non-connection is standard but uncited here. The KMS imaginary-time characterization of equilibrium is carried under formalism with its Stage-2 primary chain

limits.claim: Strict irreversibility exists only in the many-mode/thermodynamic (continuum) limit: finite closed systems recur (Poincare), with recurrence time growing with mode number
limits.source: archive: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md section 3 (closed-form independent-boson demonstration) and section 4 citing Caldeira & Leggett, Physica A 121, 587 (1983)
limits.caveat: Caldeira-Leggett cite independently confirmed 2026-09-23 (Physica A 121(3), 587-616, doi:10.1016/0378-4371(83)90013-4 — influence-functional quantum Brownian motion). The specific t_rec-proportional-to-N scaling formerly stated in this claim is the archive's own independent-boson demonstration (calc/arrow_origin.py) — PROGRAM-RESULT-grade, in-house, unreviewed — and was moved out of the COMMUNITY-DERIVED claim text by the verification pass 2026-09-23

known_connections.claim: thermodynamics EMERGES_FROM coarse-graining — CLOSED at the effective layer
known_connections.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 3 'thermodynamics ──EMERGES_FROM──▶ coarse-graining [T] CLOSED at effective layer'
known_connections.caveat: effective-layer closure only; the boundary-condition input is recorded separately

known_connections.claim: arrow-of-time REQUIRES boundary condition — INPUT (the past hypothesis), origin UNRESOLVED
known_connections.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 3 edge, imported verbatim with archive vocabulary per CORPUS_SCHEMA rule 3
known_connections.caveat: edge label is archive vocabulary, not a Stage-4 requirement extraction

known_connections.claim: Hamiltonian mechanics is equivalent to determinism plus reversibility: conservation of phase-space area (zero flow over closed regions, equivalently entropy/information conservation) is exactly a one-to-one map between past and future states
known_connections.source: Carcassi & Aidala, Found. Phys. 52, 40 (2022), arXiv:2111.09107 — full-text extraction 2026-09-23 ('Hamiltonian evolution for one degree of freedom is exactly the evolution for which the flow over a closed region in phase space is zero')
known_connections.caveat: stated exactly for one degree of freedom in the extracted passage; the paper's general program extends it

known_disconnects.claim: Dynamics-intrinsic structure does NOT fix the direction of relaxation: spectral positivity fixes |Im Sigma_R| (magnitude), never the sign; a legal population-inverted (beta < 0) KMS state reverses the arrow
known_disconnects.source: archive ref: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md sections 2, 5 ('intrinsic ceiling ... closed within the cases surveyed')
known_disconnects.caveat: scoped to equilibrium-KMS and surveyed NESS bath classes; explicitly not a universal no-go theorem; in-house, unreviewed

known_disconnects.claim: Molecular chaos (Stosszahlansatz) does NOT follow from dynamics: entangled high-correlation initial states of two thermal systems permit heat flow from colder to hotter, reversing the thermodynamic arrow
known_disconnects.source: Partovi, Phys. Rev. E 77, 021110 (2008) — title/venue/claim verified 2026-09-23 via APS listing ('a condition that is opposite to molecular chaos and shown to be unlikely in a low-entropy environment')
known_disconnects.caveat: constructed state class; shown unlikely in low-entropy environments, which is exactly the boundary-condition point

open_problems.claim: Origin of the low-entropy initial condition
open_problems.source: archive: REALITY_PICTURE_01 LEVEL 0 not-directly-observed list ('the origin of the low-entropy initial condition') + LEVEL 6 item 4 ('Initial-condition origin (arrow of time): boundary input [T]')

open_problems.claim: No dynamics-only or single-scalar route to a direction of time was found in the surveyed reduction classes
open_problems.source: archive ref: origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md section 5 — recorded not-derived, scoped to the surveyed cases
open_problems.caveat: program-scoped absence, not a community no-go theorem

open_problems.claim: No rigorous proof of eigenstate thermalization for generic interacting Hamiltonians; integrable and many-body-localized systems fail to thermalize conventionally
open_problems.source: Stage 2: cite D'Alessio, Kafri, Polkovnikov & Rigol, Adv. Phys. 65, 239 (2016) and Nandkishore & Huse, Annu. Rev. Condens. Matter Phys. 6, 15 (2015) at abstract level
open_problems.caveat: absence claim is community-standard but needs the review citations checked

observables.claim: Temperature, heat capacities, equations of state, transport coefficients, fluctuation/noise spectra (Brownian motion, Johnson-Nyquist noise), and work distributions
observables.source: Stage 2: itemize with primary citations (calorimetry standards; Perrin 1908-1909 Brownian record confirming Einstein 1905; Johnson 1928 / Nyquist 1928; noise thermometry)
observables.caveat: coarse tranche entry; the single-molecule work-distribution item already has a VERIFIED anchor under phenomena (Collin et al. 2005)

alternative_formulations.claim: Axiomatic thermodynamics from the adiabatic-accessibility order relation — entropy and temperature without statistical mechanics
alternative_formulations.source: Lieb & Yngvason, Phys. Rep. 310, 1 (1999), arXiv:cond-mat/9708200 — abstract verified 2026-09-23

alternative_formulations.claim: Reverse-Physics formulation: current laws rederived from identified physical starting assumptions, in analogy with reverse mathematics
alternative_formulations.source: Carcassi & Aidala, Found. Phys. 52, 40 (2022), arXiv:2111.09107 — abstract verified 2026-09-23
alternative_formulations.caveat: a foundations program, peer-reviewed but not community-consensus canon. Further standard framings (Jaynes maximum-entropy, Phys. Rev. 106, 620 (1957); Seifert stochastic thermodynamics, Rep. Prog. Phys. 75, 126001 (2012)) are named for Stage 2 rather than entered uncited

domain_of_validity.claim: Classical thermodynamic laws hold for macroscopic systems near equilibrium; the fluctuation-theorem extension covers small driven systems where fluctuations are comparable to mean work, verified down to single molecules
domain_of_validity.source: Collin et al., Nature 437, 231 (2005) (experimental); Crooks, Phys. Rev. E 60, 2721 (1999) (theoretical scope: stochastic, microscopically reversible dynamics)
domain_of_validity.caveat: quantum-coherent work statistics beyond two-point measurement schemes remain an active edge, uncited here

domain_of_validity.claim: KMS/detailed-balance machinery applies to equilibrium baths only: T <= 0 is KMS-undefined, and non-KMS baths (squeezed, driven-Floquet, active) relax to nonequilibrium steady states with no single beta
domain_of_validity.source: archive ref: origin/v4:gate/kms.py (T<=0 rejection) and origin/v4:ARROW_OF_TIME.md section 5
domain_of_validity.caveat: the boundary statement is community-standard physics; entered as PROGRAM-RESULT because its recorded form here is the archive's gate and survey; in-house, unreviewed
